reason: Once the Responsio was found, the first reading's doubtful words were reread against the printed text. This corrected expansions such as 'Mt. viii' and 'contradictoria', placed the column B and second-side remains in the text's order, and showed the unnumbered 'Item' where the prints number the objections.

text:
Source-assisted reading of F-f14r (Stams, Frg. 224). Reread on the native images at reading size, with the printed Responsio of Nicholas of Lyra at hand.
- Canvas 0: every line of the complete column (box 1680,1580,1240,3150) and the line openings of the second column (2880,1500,420,3350).
- Canvas 1: the first sixteen line openings of the main column (1930,1600,1070,850).
- A second research reader read, before seeing the source, the canvas 1 main-column openings at 1930,2430,870,1220 and the left-column line-ends at 1600,1550,360,2150. Those are given at the end.
- The right half of the canvas 1 main column is water-stained and unread.

Boxes are x,y,width,height in native pixels; y values are approximate. (x) expansion, [ ] lost or supplied, ? doubtful, | joint between the two strips.
